title: Red Horse Chestnut: Ancient Chestnuts You Can Visit
meta_description: A hybrid bred for pink flowers, not conkers. Three mapped so far, from a Leeuwarden hospital garden to a Bronx lawn a Van Cortlandt may have planted.
intro: The red horse chestnut is a cross bred deliberately, joining the white-flowered chestnut of every European avenue with a red-flowered American buckeye, first recorded in Germany around 1820. The result flowers pink in May instead of white, sets almost no spiny conkers, and shrugs off the leaf miner moth that browns out its white parent by late summer. It was planted for gardens, not found in the wild, which shows in where these three stand: a former hospital courtyard in Leeuwarden whose tree survived 1990s redevelopment with crown anchors and a trunk wound to show for it, a public square in Amstelveen with no history recorded at all, and the lawn of a 1748 house in the Bronx, where family tradition says a Van Cortlandt planted it themselves. Three trees, three very different kinds of care.
